name: NMUX1308PWJ
title: 1.5 V to 5.5 V 8-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer with injection-current control
summary: The NMUX1308 is a CMOS single-pole eight-throw analog switch: three select lines and an active-LOW enable connect one of Y0 to Y7 to the common pin Z, in either direction, with signals from GND to VCC on a 1.5 V to 5.5 V supply. Every analog pin has a shunt that steers current forced above VCC or below GND into ground, so an overdriven off channel barely disturbs the one that is on. The control inputs keep 1.8 V logic thresholds at any supply and tolerate 5.5 V, and with VCC at 0 V neither control nor analog pins feed the supply. It replaces 4051 and 4851 parts pin for pin.

circuits.title: Eight signals multiplexed into a microcontroller's ADC
circuits.description: Eight sensor or voltage signals land on Y0 to Y7. The microcontroller drives S0, S1, S2 and E from four I/O lines to pick which one reaches Z. Z feeds an op amp wired as a voltage follower (output tied back to its inverting input), and the follower's output drives the microcontroller's built-in SAR ADC. The buffer gives the ADC the low source impedance it wants when a signal source is high impedance, and keeps the ADC's input leakage from dropping a voltage across the switch. One capacitor bypasses VCC to ground at the pin; pin 7 is open. The scheme lets one ADC input read eight channels.

circuits.title: Multiplexer followed by a non-inverting gain stage
circuits.description: The same eight-input arrangement with Z driving the non-inverting input of an op amp. R3 runs from the inverting input to ground and R4 from the output back to the inverting input, so the selected signal is amplified by 1 + R4/R3 and appears at VOUT. VCC is bypassed to ground at the pin; the select and enable lines come from outside.

operation.text: With E LOW, S2 S1 S0 read as a binary number pick the channel: LLL joins Y0 to Z, HHH joins Y7 to Z. E HIGH opens all eight regardless of the select lines. Each path conducts both ways with the same characteristics, so the part works as a multiplexer or a demultiplexer. Opening one channel completes at least 1 ns before the next closes.

A voltage spike on an analog line that goes above VCC pushes current into the pin, and one below GND pulls current out. Each analog pin, selected or not, has a bypass FET to GND that carries both kinds away, so the supply stays put, RON stays put and the selected channel's output moves by only a fraction of a millivolt to a few millivolts (ΔVO). An injected current of -25 mA to 50 mA per off switch, and ±100 mA across all off switches, is allowed; no external clamp network is needed.

S0, S1, S2 and E keep thresholds compatible with 1.8 V logic over the full 1.5 V to 5.5 V supply range (VIH 1.32 V min at VCC = 5 V), so a low-voltage controller drives them directly. They accept up to 5.5 V at any supply, so a 5 V signal can drive them while VCC is lower.

The ESD diodes on control and analog pins have no path to VCC. With VCC at 0 V the pins stay high impedance: leakage is small, no biased pin powers the supply rail, and the switch stays open. Analog pins may sit at 0 V to 5.5 V while VCC = 0 V.
E, S0, S1 and S2 must each be driven or tied; none may float.

Decouple VCC with a low-ESR ceramic capacitor of 0.1 µF or more (X5R, X7R or NP0) close to the pin, and take GND to a solid ground plane. A second, larger capacitor can be added farther out, the smaller one (typically 0402) nearest the pin, to cover both low- and high-frequency noise. Run switched signals over unbroken ground; a small ground pour between traces cuts crosstalk. Traces turn only in 45° or serpentine bends, never 90°.
The centre pad is not a supply connection and has no electrical or mechanical need to be soldered; a soldered land is left floating or tied to GND.
